title: Git hooks silently no-op when only .entire/settings.local.json exists (entire enable --local)

verdict.rationale: IsSetUp was written to check only settings.json and noted as such, and IsSetUpAndEnabled was built on it to make hooks a no-op when Entire isn't enabled. Later, IsSetUpAny was added for the setup flow, but the evidence shows no decision that hooks should ignore a settings.local.json-only setup; that case was simply never considered.

quotes.quote: Good — `IsSetUp` only checks `settings.json`, and it's only used by `IsSetUpAndEnabled` which is used in hooks. For the new flow I need a broader check that includes `settings.local.json`.

# Plan: Add Context Plumbing Throughout the CLI

## Context

`main.go` creates a cancellable context (`context.WithCancel`) and passes it to Cobra via `rootCmd.ExecuteContext(ctx)`. However, no command retrieves it via `cmd.Context()`. Instead, ~120+ production code locations create `context.Background()`, losing cancellation support from SIGINT/SIGTERM and any parent context values.

## Goal

Thread the root context from `main.go` through the entire call chain, replacing `context.Background()` with the properly propagated context. This enables signal-based cancellation to propagate to git operations, checkpoint writes, and other long-running work.
